title: Disjoint Sets: Union-Find with Amortised Analysis

blocks.text: Imagine managing a network of computers where you need to efficiently determine if two computers are in the same network. This is the essence of the union-find problem.

blocks.markdown: The union-find data structure, also known as disjoint set union (DSU), is a fundamental structure used to manage a partition of a set into disjoint subsets. It supports two primary operations: **find**, which determines the subset a particular element is in, and **union**, which merges two subsets into a single subset.

blocks.title: Union-Find Operations
blocks.text: The two main operations in union-find are: 1. **Find(x)**: Returns the root of the set containing element x. 2. **Union(x, y)**: Merges the sets containing elements x and y.

blocks.markdown: To optimize these operations, we use two techniques: **union by rank** and **path compression**. Union by rank ensures that the smaller tree is always added under the root of the larger tree, while path compression flattens the structure of the tree whenever **find** is called.

blocks.title: Amortised Analysis
blocks.text: Amortised analysis helps us understand the average time complexity of operations over a sequence, rather than the worst-case time of a single operation.

blocks.caption: The amortised time complexity of union-find operations with path compression and union by rank is $O(\alpha(n))$, where $\alpha(n)$ is the inverse Ackermann function.

blocks.title: Example of Union by Rank and Path Compression
blocks.prompt: Consider a set of elements {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Perform the following operations: Union(1, 2), Union(3, 4), Union(2, 3), Find(4). Trace the changes in the structure.

steps.text: Start with each element in its own set: {1}, {2}, {3}, {4}, {5}.
Union(1, 2): Merge sets {1} and {2}. Using union by rank, attach the smaller tree under the larger one.
Find(4): Path compression occurs, flattening the tree structure.

blocks.answer: After all operations, the sets are {1, 2, 3, 4} and {5}. The tree structure is flattened for elements 1 to 4.

blocks.markdown: Path compression significantly speeds up the **find** operation by making the tree shallower, which reduces the time complexity for future operations.

blocks.title: Amortised Cost Calculation
blocks.prompt: Calculate the amortised cost of a sequence of 10 union and 10 find operations on a set of 10 elements.

steps.text: Each union operation takes $O(\alpha(n))$ time due to union by rank.
Each find operation takes $O(\alpha(n))$ time due to path compression.
For 10 union and 10 find operations, the total cost is $20 \times O(\alpha(n))$.
Since $\alpha(n)$ grows very slowly, the cost is nearly constant for practical input sizes.

blocks.answer: The amortised cost for 20 operations is $20 \times O(\alpha(n))$, which is nearly constant.

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.text: Do not confuse the amortised complexity with worst-case complexity. Amortised complexity gives an average over a sequence of operations.

points: Union-find is optimized using union by rank and path compression.
Amortised analysis shows near-constant average time complexity for operations.
